SMG Amirullah Chowdhury with Abul Hossain Azadi, Advocates -For the Appellants

parties:
Zahed alias Zahed Ali & ors ------ Appellants
Vs.
State ------ Respondent
full_judgment: 13. Now, when the appellants have been charged under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code specifically on the allegations that the appellants committed murder of the victim in furtherance of common intention we feel in the facts and circumstances of the case application of section 460 of the Penal Code in the charge is materially defective. In this connection some decisions are referred before us by Mr Chowdhury, reported in AIR 1954 (Madras) 152; PLD 1956 (Lahore) 157. In the case of Singaram and another reported in AIR 1954 (Madras) 152; it has been observed by a Division Bench that "Section 460 can be invoked only if, from the evidence, it is clearly possible to conclude that before the commission of the lurking house trespass by night, or house-breaking by night, the offenders did not have a common intention of committing anything other than the above mentioned offences and that if during the course of the commission of such an offence one of the persons causes death or grievous hurt to any person, then only, every person jointly concerned in committing lurking house-trespass by night or house-breaking by night shall be guilty of an offence under section 460 IPC. If, on other evidence, Court is satisfied that the accused are guilty of murder then section 466 IPC is out of place. In such case the invocation of section 460 is irregular". In the case of Fateh Sher and another vs Crown, reported in PLD 1956 (Lahore) 157, it has been observed that the offence of murder having been committed after the offence of house-breaking terminated, will not attract the provision of section 460 PC and held that section 460 was inapplicable. Thus it appears that invoking of section 460 of the Penal Code along with the charge under sections 302/34, Penal Code is irregular, improper and defective in this case. Of course, it does not appear in the instant case that the appellants have been prejudiced for such inclusion of section 460, Penal Code in the charge, though, by the conviction and sentence under section 460, Penal Code they have been greatly prejudiced. In our view, in the facts and circumstances of the case, when the appellants have been charged under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code and convicted and sentenced there under, their conviction and sentences at the same time under section 460 Penal Code in the same case is bad in law and should be set aside in view of the misjoinder of the charge.
